title: Personal Page
text:
Hello!
Welcome to my webpage! I am currently a PhD candidate in mathematics / probability at INRIA in the MATHNET Team under the supervision of Bartek Blaszczsyn (INRIA) and  Julien de Rosny  (Institut Langevin). My PhD is funded by the PSL Grand Projet Smart Waves  under the name “GeoSto4RIS”.
I work on probabilistic models arising in wireless networks. Currently my research focuses on continuum percolation and their applications to telecommunications.

title: About
text:
Interests
My main academic interests are currently stochastic geometry (very vague…) and continuum percolation, but I am just beginning and hopefully I can discover new things!
I would like to know a little bit more Statistics and learn about Optimal Transport which are topics which interest me. Besides maths, I am currently quite interested in economics but I have yet to pick up a book on it…
Outside research, I am also interested in (non-exhaustive list) playing Chess, doing a bit of sports, listening to a lot of music, watching esports, reading (currently reading “The Dawn of Everything” which is extremely interesting!).
I am obsessed with making good-looking figures in Python for my papers. It can take me hours but I love it…

title: Research
text:
Current projects

Non-trivial phase transition for the Visibility-Relay Model for \(d = 2\)
Currently we’re finalizing a paper with my supervisor proving the existence of a phase transition for the Visibility-Relay Model which we introduced to model Line of Sight communication network in random environments. This work is reminiscent of the article by Hirsch, Janel & Cali (Continuum percolation for Cox point processes). The arguments follow roughly the same structure but some of their techniques do not work for our case and we find other solutions.
I will be presenting this  poster  in Rouen for the  GeoSto26 conference.

title: Research
text:
Past Projects

Master Thesis
In this thesis we discuss various results relating to Central Limit Theorems for Point Process. We first go over the cumulants method and its theoretical basis. Secondly, we study perturbed hyper-uniform Point Processes by \(\alpha\)-stable perturbation and determine a condition under which the new process is still hyper-uniform and its new hyper-uniform exponent.
